title: Region voting orchestrator: combine p50/p95 latency and network health for tiered routing and variant fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a region 'voting' orchestrator that synthesizes short- and long-tail latency telemetry (p50/p95) with a network health score to decide region preference, tier routing, and when to trigger model-variant fallbacks. The goal is to reduce user-facing p95 latency regressions during transient network degradation while minimizing unnecessary cross-region routing and cost. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, hysteresis, rollout gating, telemetry instrumentation, and automation hooks for fallbacks to compatible model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Production traffic uses the new orchestrator behind a feature flag for 10% of requests in staging and 5% in canary within EU/NA regions
Observed p95 for canary traffic improves (or at least does not regress) compared to baseline during induced link blips in test harness
False-positive region switches (flip-flop) are <1% over 1h windows during steady-state traffic
Fallback to model-variant occurs only when composite score crosses hard threshold and compatible variant is available; fallback rate tracked and limited via quota
Telemetry exposes new Grafana panels: region_vote_reason, region_score_breakdown, fallback_trigger_rate, routing_delta_cost
Documentation (Confluence) updated with algorithm, thresholds, and runbook steps for manual override
design_notes: Composite region score = weighted sum: 0.6 * normalized p95 + 0.25 * normalized p50 + 0.15 * normalized network_health_penalty (higher penalty = worse). Scores normalized to 0-100 where lower is better.

Network health score constructed from packet loss (30%), connection_fail_rate (35%), retransmit_rate (20%), node_err_rate (15%). Each submetric uses EWMA with 1m and 15m windows to capture spikes and sustained issues.

Two-window decision rule: require both short window (1m) and medium window (15m) to exceed thresholds before switching to a different region or triggering fallback; short window triggers fast-weight but requires medium window confirmation to avoid noise.
Hysteresis: on-change cooldown of 120s + exponential backoff for repeated flips. Minimum stable time in new region = 3 minutes before reconsideration.

Tier routing: prefer same-tier region first. If preferred region's score is degraded and fallback_count < 2, route to next healthy same-tier region. If no same-tier healthy region exists, route to lower-tier variant in same-region (model variant) to meet latency SLOs.

Model-variant fallback constraints: only switch to variants flagged as 'latency-first compatible' and passing recent quality-eval smoke tests. Annotate model catalog with compatibility tags and quality thresholds.
Cost control: include cost_penalty factor to avoid aggressive cross-region routing for small latency wins. Default cost weight is 0.05; operable via console tuning.
Telemetry sampling: full telemetry for 1% sample by default, dynamic increase to 10% on detected anomalies to aid debugging.
Rollout will be feature-flagged per-customer and per-route via console; default OFF for high-SLA enterprise accounts until validated.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): unit and integration tests + synthetic chaos tests (packet loss, latency spikes) against region routing harness
Phase 1 (canary): enable 5% traffic in US-EAST and EU-WEST for non-enterprise customers; monitor region_vote_reason and fallback_trigger_rate for 72h
Phase 2 (slow rollout): ramp up to 30% over 2 days with automated rollback if p95 regression > 8% or fallback rate > 0.5% of routed traffic
Phase 3: opt-in enterprise beta with manual audit and support on-call present; default OFF for dedicated/private hosts until validators run
Emergency rollback: feature flag kill switch in console + runtime override endpoint to pin region per customer or route
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization boundaries
Integration tests: end-to-end routing decision path with mocked telemetry inputs (steady, spike, sustained degradation)
Chaos tests in staging: inject packet loss (1-10%), connection resets, and node error storms to confirm hysteresis behaves and fallbacks trigger appropriately
A/B test harness: synthetic traffic plus a small % of real traffic to measure user latency and correctness across variants
Load test: ensure orchestrator decision latency < 5ms added to request routing path under 10k qps
Quality regression: run prompt-eval suite on any candidate model-variant to ensure fallback doesn't regress output quality beyond configured threshold
